t: iOS App Builder - public implementations survey
title: iOS App Builder - public implementations survey
definition: Builds applications for compatible Apple mobile environments.
description:
iOS App Builder is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Builds applications for compatible Apple mobile environments. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns iOS App Builder. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves iOS App Builder. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the iOS App Builder capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

t: Expo - related iOS App Builder technology
title: Expo - related iOS App Builder technology
definition: Managed React Native workflow.
description:
Expo is not itself an iOS App Builder, but it belongs in this survey because real iOS App Builder work leans on it. Managed React Native workflow.

In an iOS App Builder build it shows up when startup speed beats raw peak power. Its architecture reflects hard-won lessons: small sharp pieces, explicit contracts between them, and no magic hidden from the operator. Knowing the surrounding technology is part of knowing the capability - the best iOS App Builder practitioners can say exactly where their tool ends and its neighbors begin.

For builders, Expo is a strong default choice as supporting technology. The demo program exercises a core idea from its domain - run it with node and watch each step.

t: iOS App Builder review checklist - practitioner discipline

description:
review checklist is the iOS App Builder discipline: Builds applications for compatible Apple mobile environments. It turns iOS App Builder from an event into a repeatable capability.

In practice this means: keep a failure log: what broke, why, and what now prevents it; review the result with fresh eyes before calling it done; declare inputs, expected outputs, and acceptance checks before starting Teams that follow the discipline get predictable builds; teams that skip it get interesting stories. The Signature line prefers predictable builds, and this record's demo makes the discipline concrete and runnable.

t: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of iOS App Builder f
title: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of iOS App Builder f
definition: Ladder drill (foundation): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of iOS App Builder from a one-paragraph brief.
description:
Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of iOS App Builder from a one-paragraph brief

Read the brief twice. List every input the iOS App Builder needs, every output it must produce, and one contract each input-output pair must satisfy. Work it by hand first, then run the demo program and compare its trace against your own reasoning. When they agree, the concept is yours.

Success criterion: you can list them from memory without looking at the brief
